From 7d9a7f1f96cd617ee9e75bb22217c709038e26b8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ye Bin <yebin10@huawei.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 21:14:18 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] smb/client: fix possible infinite loop and oob read in
 symlink_data()

On 32-bit architectures, the infinite loop is as follows:

  len = p->ErrorDataLength == 0xfffffff8
  u8 *next = p->ErrorContextData + len
  next == p

On 32-bit architectures, the out-of-bounds read is as follows:

  len = p->ErrorDataLength == 0xfffffff0
  u8 *next = p->ErrorContextData + len
  next == (u8 *)p - 8

Reported-by: ChenXiaoSong <chenxiaosong@kylinos.cn>
Fixes: 76894f3e2f71 ("cifs: improve symlink handling for smb2+")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ye Bin <yebin10@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: ChenXiaoSong <chenxiaosong@kylinos.cn>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <stfrench@microsoft.com>

diff --git a/fs/smb/client/smb2file.c b/fs/smb/client/smb2file.c
index b292aa94a593..6860eff31693 100644
--- a/fs/smb/client/smb2file.c
+++ b/fs/smb/client/smb2file.c
@@ -49,6 +49,9 @@ static struct smb2_symlink_err_rsp *symlink_data(const struct kvec *iov)
 				 __func__, le32_to_cpu(p->ErrorId));
 
 			len = ALIGN(le32_to_cpu(p->ErrorDataLength), 8);
+			if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p)))
+				return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);
+
 			p = (struct smb2_error_context_rsp *)(p->ErrorContextData + len);
 		}
 	} else if (le32_to_cpu(err->ByteCount) >= sizeof(*sym) &&
-- 
2.34.1

The patch consists of a single modification in the file `fs/smb/client/smb2file.c`. The change adds a bounds check inside the `symlink_data()` function to prevent an infinite loop and an out-of-bounds read that could occur on 32-bit architectures due to integer arithmetic issues.

**Modifications in `fs/smb/client/smb2file.c`:**  
- After calculating `len = ALIGN(le32_to_cpu(p->ErrorDataLength), 8)`, a validation is inserted:  
  ```c
  if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p)))
      return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);
  ```  
  This ensures that the computed length does not exceed the remaining buffer space (from the current `p` to the buffer `end`). If it does, the function returns an error (`-EINVAL`) instead of proceeding with an invalid pointer.

**Relationship:**  
The added check directly addresses the root cause of both the infinite loop and the out-of-bounds read. Without it, when `ErrorDataLength` is a large value (e.g., `0xfffffff8` or `0xfffffff0`), the ALIGN calculation can cause `len` to wrap around or point to an address equal to or before `p`. This leads to the loop either never advancing (infinite loop) or reading memory before the buffer (out-of-bounds read). By validating that `len` fits in the remaining space before updating `p`, the patch ensures safe iteration through error context responses.
